statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail 5 (low) in every hour of the CME weekend halt; Stress 25 (moderate); Confidence 64 (solid).
recommendation: Descriptive only. CME Globex has been halted since Friday 21:00 UTC and does not reopen until Sunday 30 August at 22:00 UTC, so no Nasdaq-100 price path can form in any hour of this window and Tail remains far below the block threshold for both NQ_FUTURES and NAS100_CFD. Stress runs 25 to 38 in the moderate band as unpriced weekend information accumulates ahead of the 1 to 4 September data stack, and Confidence declines from 64 to a 60 floor purely because the reference tape ages rather than because the evidence has become conflicting. No danger window is published, because the first hour in which observable Nasdaq-100 structure can exist falls beyond the end of this forecast.
headline: Weekend halt, hour 25: NDX 29,433.43 (-0.70%), NQ 29,491.75, VIX 14.43, the 10-year near 4.72% and a coin-flip September Fed meeting after Warsh; Globex reopens Sunday 22:00 UTC
body: CME Globex has been halted since Friday 21:00 UTC and does not reopen until Sunday 30 August at 22:00 UTC, so every hour of this forecast window is a closed venue with no Nasdaq-100 price discovery; NQ last traded at 20:59 UTC on 28 August and the scheduled reopen falls about an hour after this window closes. The pre-halt evidence set was re-verified against primary sources this run: cash NDX closed 29,433.43, down 0.70 percent or 208.13 points, inside a 29,383.92 to 29,752.78 range against a 29,641.56 previous close; NQ futures last printed 29,491.75, down 0.69 percent or 204.00 points, in a 29,436.75 to 29,811.50 range against a 29,695.75 previous close; VIX finished at 14.43 within a 14.13 to 14.84 range against a 14.51 previous close. The dominant driver remains Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole keynote, read as hawkish: current reporting describes the September meeting as close to a coin flip, with hike odds repriced into a roughly 54 to 59 percent range from about 34 to 35 percent beforehand, and the policy-sensitive 2-year yield rising on the day while the 10-year was quoted near 4.72 percent. The Federal Reserve H.15 daily release still carries 27 August as its most recent column, at 4.20 percent for the 2-year and 4.67 percent for the 10-year, because the release is not posted at weekends. Friday's decline was narrow rather than broad: the semiconductor industry fell 2.91 percent and semiconductor equipment 3.96 percent, led by Arm down 6.33 percent and Nvidia down 4.57 percent, while five of eight tracked megacaps advanced, with Amazon up 3.97 percent, Alphabet up 1.74 percent and Microsoft up 1.68 percent, leaving megacap dispersion near 2.5 percentage points. Energy was orderly into the weekend, with WTI at 83.44 dollars and Brent at 88.29 dollars, and no fresh verified supply discontinuity was identified in this run's geopolitical check. Weekend information flow has been commentary rather than event risk: verified items include the Jackson Hole coverage of 28 August, the same day's reporting on the repricing of rate-hike expectations, and Saturday's published commentary from Adam Posen on the Fed's communication of a forecast. None of that can reach a price until the venue reopens. Tail is therefore held at 5 in all 24 slots, which maps to EA_ON and green throughout and publishes no danger window, because a closed market cannot produce the shallow pullbacks, failed retracements, repeated extension or session-extreme holding that Tail measures. Stress rises from 25 to 38 inside the moderate band as the stock of unpriced weekend information grows ahead of the reopen and the 1 to 4 September data stack. Confidence eases from 64 to a 60 floor, remaining in the solid band because the evidence is complete and primary-source verified and is ageing rather than becoming conflicted.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours cover the final hour of Friday's cash session, the post-close futures hour and hours one through twenty-four of the weekend halt. The mode was mixed in the 21:00 UTC Friday block, with Tail 8 and Stress 30 as the Jackson Hole keynote was still being digested, and the mapped policy state never exceeded EA_ON because retracements kept occurring throughout the repricing. After the close the mode settled to normal and Tail decayed from 7 to 5, where it stayed for every subsequent hour. Stress fell to a 22 trough in the early hours of Saturday and then held a 25 plateau for the last sixteen hours, while Confidence declined steadily from 86 to 65 as the reference tape aged without any new observable structure. No hour in the window carried a danger window and no hour was unavailable.
outlookSummary: Every hour of the forecast window falls inside the CME weekend halt, so no Nasdaq-100 price path can form; Tail is held at 5 in all 24 slots, keeping the mapped policy state at EA_ON throughout with no danger window, and the dominant mode is normal in every slot because a closed market has no structure to classify rather than because conditions are assessed as calm. Stress ramps from 25 to 38 in the moderate band, rising with the stock of unpriced weekend information ahead of a reopen at Sunday 22:00 UTC that falls about an hour after the window closes, and ahead of the 1 to 4 September data stack of ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS, ADP, Broadcom results, ISM Services and the August payrolls report, with the 15 to 16 September FOMC meeting priced close to a coin flip behind it. Confidence eases from 64 to a 60 floor, staying in the solid band because the evidence set is complete and primary-source verified even as the reference tape ages past forty-seven hours by the final slot. The first hour in which observable Nasdaq-100 structure can exist lies beyond this window, so any gap or continuation at the reopen is a checkpoint for a later assessment rather than a published risk here.
